text: The Sun's mahadasha is the shortest of the nine Vedic chapters, six years spent on who you are and where you stand. Every such chapter is shared out among the nine lords in turn, and each lord's stretch of it is called an antardasha. This one belongs to Ketu. Ketu is the Moon's south node, the backward-facing eclipse point, and it has almost no interest in applause. The chapter's business goes on, but your appetite for it can thin. A role you worked hard for may start to feel like a costume. Recognition arrives and lands quietly, or fails to arrive and bothers you less than you expected it would. Some people step back in this run: they hand off a title, close a public project, or stop performing a version of themselves they had outgrown. Others keep the position and change what it is for. Attention turns inward or backward. Questions you set aside years ago come around again, and so do people and projects you had counted as finished. Solitary work goes well, while anything that requires constant visibility can feel like a tax on the day. Parents, employers, and other figures of authority may grow distant, in fact or in feeling. Energy often runs below the chapter's usual pitch, so the pace deserves respect rather than argument. The risk is walking away from something that still deserves you and calling it detachment. Held honestly, the run takes a decoration or two off your standing and leaves you clearer about what sits underneath.

Venus takes an antardasha here, a shorter run inside the Sun's six-year chapter, and it brings company to a stretch otherwise concerned with standing alone. Classical Vedic texts count these two as an uneasy pair, which in practice tends to show up less as trouble than as a change of priorities. Pleasure gets a vote in a season that mostly wanted results. Relationships move up the agenda. A partnership may begin or deepen, an old affection may reopen, and your social circle can widen exactly when your public life is asking for focus. Good things often arrive through people who like you rather than through effort: an introduction, an invitation, a favor nobody wrote down. Comfort and earnings tend to improve, and taste sharpens. If you make anything, this run flatters the finished surface of it, the part other people see and enjoy. The pull to be liked is what to watch. The chapter wants you saying what you actually think, and Venus is very good at smoothing that into something easier to hear. You may soften a position to keep a room pleasant, or take flattery where respect was the thing you needed. Ease can also slow the chapter down, since it is simple to enjoy the view and stop climbing. Taken well, the stretch corrects a common error about authority. It shows you that a position carried warmly loses none of its weight, and that being pleasant to deal with is not the same as being negotiable.

The Sun's chapter opens with itself. In the Vedic sequence a mahadasha is a major planetary period, and it is divided among the nine lords in a fixed order, each holding a stretch called an antardasha, with the lord of the chapter always first. Six years of Sun therefore begin at full strength, with nothing else mixed in. This run usually declares the theme. Something asks you to step forward: a promotion, a public piece of work, a decision only you can sign, or a plain refusal to keep deferring to somebody. Confidence rises, and so does the wish to be taken seriously by people whose seriousness you respect. Vitality belongs to the picture too, and many readers pay real attention to their energy for the first time in years. Authority appears in every form. You may deal with officials, employers, or a parent whose authority still carries weight, and long-standing arrangements with any of them can get renegotiated on adult terms. Where your life has been running on somebody else's permission, this stretch tends to expose the arrangement. The trouble is that nothing softens the light. Certainty hardens fast, criticism lands as insult, and a stubborn stand can cost more than the point was worth. It helps to remember how young the chapter is. What starts here generally sets the direction of the years that follow, so the honest use of the run is to put your name on something you would still defend after the glare moves elsewhere.

Now the other light takes a turn. A mahadasha is the major Vedic chapter and an antardasha is a sub-period inside it, and the Moon's softens six years otherwise given to rank and reputation. The two lights keep different time. The Sun stays put; the Moon is never the same twice in a month, so advancement in this run arrives in waves. A strong stretch is followed by a doubtful one, and confidence has to be rebuilt more than once. Nothing has gone wrong when that happens. It is how the season moves. Private life presses in. Questions of house and household get loud, and people often move, remodel, or rearrange who lives with whom. A parent, or whoever filled that role early on, tends to feature, sometimes through care needed and sometimes through a shift in how you understand what they gave you. Feeling becomes information you cannot ignore, which makes this a good run for work that depends on reading a room. It is also a warm stretch with the public, since the old texts give the Moon the mood of the many. Work aimed at ordinary people rather than at gatekeepers usually finds its audience. The difficulty is thin skin under a bright light. Criticism goes deeper than it should, and plain tiredness can pass itself off as failure. Rest counts as work here. What the run adds to the chapter is a standing with some comfort in it, and a domestic life sturdy enough to hold the rest of the years.

Mars holds the antardasha, one lord's turn at running a stretch of the Sun's six years, and the temperature climbs. The tradition counts these two as friends, and the pairing often does feel like an alliance. The chapter wants you visible, Mars wants you moving, and between them they favor the direct route. Matters you have been circling get decided. People use this run to push a project into the open, take a demanding role, force a stalled negotiation, or leave a place they had outgrown. Effort turns into result faster than it does in the slower stretches. Ambition stops being embarrassing. You may want the promotion out loud, or compete for something you would normally pretend not to care about. Physical energy usually runs high and wants a use, so training, building, and hard practical work all suit the run. Conflict comes with the package. Friction with people in authority is the classic form, and under the Sun such quarrels tend to have witnesses. Anger does good work in a task and expensive damage to a person whose good opinion you will want next year. Haste is the other hazard, along with a body asked for more than it has been given, so pace matters more than nerve. Used well, the stretch converts nerve into evidence. Having contested something in the open and lived through the noise, you carry the remaining years of the chapter with less flinch in you.

Rahu takes the antardasha now, its turn at part of the larger chapter, and the tradition treats this as the strangest of the nine pairings. Rahu is the Moon's north node, the leading point of the eclipse axis, and in the old images it is the mouth that swallows the Sun. Put it inside the Sun's six years and ambition tends to lose its brakes. Your reach extends further than the chapter alone would take it. People go after a bigger stage in this run: a foreign posting, an unfamiliar industry, an audience outside their usual circle, a kind of success nobody in the family attempted. The unconventional route often works better than the respectable one, and the gains can be real and quick. What is harder to trust is the picture. Rahu enlarges, so a position can look grander than it is, and the wish to be seen may fasten onto people whose opinion you do not actually value. Reputation is the tender spot, since it can grow fast and it can blur. Quick routes look better than they are under this lord, and a claim sometimes gets made before the thing behind it exists. Hunger is the honest name for what drives the stretch, and meeting a goal rarely switches it off. Kept in view rather than denied, that appetite is usable. The run tends to enlarge a life. What decides whether the enlargement lasts is how much of it you built and how much you were only standing in front of.

Jupiter's antardasha, its turn at the wheel inside the Sun's six-year chapter, is usually the kindest run of the nine. The two count as friends in this tradition, and they tend to want similar things: honest position, plain purpose, usefulness in the open. Under this lord the chapter widens. Backing tends to arrive in person. Someone senior takes an interest, vouches for you, or opens a door you had been knocking on politely for a while. Large bodies get easier to deal with, whether that means a university, a court, a publisher, or whatever counts as the big room in your line of work. Recognition in this stretch comes with weight behind it rather than noise. Teaching and being taught both go well, and a course of study begun now can change what you are trusted with. Meaning grows loud too. The chapter has been asking who you are; Jupiter asks what the position is for, and the question is hard to put off. Family often gathers or grows, and some people become a parent, a mentor, or the one others bring their problems to. The hazard is scale outrunning the foundation. Confidence runs warm, promises get made in a good mood, and a role can grow past the work holding it up. Complacency is the quieter version, since a favorable stretch is easy to spend coasting. Taken seriously, this run raises the ceiling of the whole chapter and leaves you somewhere larger, with a better account of why you wanted to be there.

Of the nine runs inside the Sun's chapter, tradition expects Saturn's to ask the most and hurry the least. An antardasha is a sub-period held by one lord inside the major period, and this one puts the slowest planet in charge of a season built for advancement. The calendar stretches. Decisions wait on other people, approvals take longer than they ought to, and payment for a piece of work often shows up a season after the work. Responsibility increases without the title keeping pace. You may carry a team, a household, or a project mostly alone, and find that your competence is being tested well before it is being paid. Elders and institutions stand out: a strict superior, a parent who needs you, rules written by people nobody has ever met. Where your standing rests on charm or timing rather than skill, this run tends to find the gap, which is uncomfortable and useful in roughly equal measure. Discouragement is the real weather of the stretch. Effort goes unremarked, energy sits below the chapter's usual level, and a slow month can start to argue that you were wrong about yourself. Keeping some warmth in the week helps more than pushing harder does, and so does treating rest as part of the job. What the run finally hands over is solidity. Nothing in it comes quickly, and the parts of your position that survive it stop needing you to defend them.

Mercury's antardasha, the stretch it governs inside the Sun's six years, turns the season talkative. These two are rarely far apart in the sky, and the pairing tends to work in your favor: the chapter concerns who you are, and Mercury governs how that gets said, written, and agreed to. Words do the heavy lifting now. Meetings, proposals, interviews, contracts, and correspondence multiply, and things get settled in documents rather than in rooms. Many people spend this run building the language for what they do, then discover that explaining it has changed it. Terms you accept here tend to govern the rest of the chapter, so the small print is worth an hour. Learning belongs to the stretch as well. A skill picked up now usually attaches to your name and keeps earning after the run closes, especially in analysis, teaching, trade, or the handling of information. Travel is short and frequent rather than far. Contacts multiply, and a sibling, or somebody who occupies that place in your life, may figure in the story. The mind moves fast in this period and sometimes past its own accuracy. Saying yes is easy when everything sounds interesting, and a confident explanation can get ahead of the evidence under it. The paperwork rarely thins out either. Kept honest, the run gives your position a vocabulary. You come out able to state your case without ornament, in terms that hold when somebody goes and checks them.
